3. **Threat Model & Security Control Evaluation (Observed):**
   - **Prompt Injection:** Comprehensive attack coverage including direct/indirect injection, schema-valid malicious candidates, action-choice/argument manipulation, confidential egress, social engineering, prompt-to-host bridges, cross-Bureau persistence, and resource exhaustion.
   - **Labeled Capability Envelope:** The selected control (`bureau-labeled-capability-envelope`) propagates security labels (`provenance`, `integrity`, `readers`, `freshness`, `scope`, `authority_ceiling`) across every context value and enforces integrity policy on action selection and security-relevant arguments, as well as permitted-flow policy on all response/egress sinks. Model outputs are strictly un-endorsed draft candidates; models receive no label management, capability, endorsement, declassification, or write power. User confirmation is maintained as a separate, signed, expiring authority act.
   - **One-Shot Brokered Cell:** The selected containment control (`one-shot-brokered-cell`) isolates each attempt into a fresh generation with one typed input and one candidate output channel. The broker owns provider transport, credentials, quotas, and hostile-byte parsing (model output is never evaluated as code). Ambient shell, code execution, host path access, sockets, metadata endpoints, databases, and actuators are denied. Teardown and residue evidence are mandatory on all terminal states.
   - **API Spine Integrity:** Read operations remain on read-only GraphQL/context frames; command execution remains restricted to REST/OpenAPI with backend reauthorization, idempotency, audit, and readback. Provider safeguards and human reviews are treated solely as defense-in-depth layers.
